+#!/usr/bin/env node
+/**
+ * headerRtlDirection.test.cjs — the Doctor header's menu button must sit at the
+ * top-RIGHT in Arabic and stay top-LEFT in English.
+ *
+ * ROOT CAUSE PINNED HERE
+ * ──────────────────────
+ * `PageHeader` mirrored its row with `flexDirection: isRTL ? 'row-reverse' : 'row'`
+ * — but `flexDirection` is NOT physical in React Native. Yoga flips the main
+ * axis whenever the LAYOUT direction is RTL, which it is on a native Arabic
+ * launch (`I18nManager.isRTL`). The unpinned `row-reverse` was therefore
+ * resolved back to left-to-right, and the hamburger rendered in the top-LEFT
+ * corner of Video Library, Students, My Balance and Notifications on iOS and
+ * Android. The web build has no Yoga direction, so it looked correct there —
+ * which is exactly why the defect survived review.
+ *
+ * The fix is the contract the rest of the app already follows: pin the row with
+ * `direction: 'ltr'` so the mirror is the ONLY one, and mirror the safe-area
+ * padding physically (the leading control clears the edge it actually sits on).
+ *
+ * WHAT THIS CHECKS
+ *   1. PageHeader mirrors the row AND pins `direction: 'ltr'`.
+ *   2. DashboardHeader does too (its right-actions row inherits the pin).
+ *   3. ResponsiveTabBar and the drawer track keep the same contract.
+ *   4. INVARIANT: no `flexDirection: isRTL ? ...` anywhere in src/ is left
+ *      unpinned — the general form of this bug.
+ *   5. PageHeader's RTL leading padding is the RIGHT inset; LTR's is the left.
+ *   6. The four reported screens render through the shared PageHeader (so the
+ *      fix reaches them and cannot drift per screen).
+ *   7. English is unchanged: the LTR branch still pins 'row'.
+ *
+ * Run: node tests/headerRtlDirection.test.cjs
+ */
+
+'use strict';
+
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const path = require('node:path');
+
+const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
+const read = (rel) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
+
+let passed = 0;
+let failed = 0;
+function check(name, cond, detail = '') {
+  if (cond) {
+    passed++;
+    console.log('  ✓ ' + name);
+  } else {
+    failed++;
+    console.error('  ✗ ' + name + (detail ? `  [${detail}]` : ''));
+  }
+}
+function section(name) {
+  console.log('\n── ' + name + ' ──');
+}
+/** Drop full-line comments so prose about the fix cannot satisfy a pin. */
+function code(src) {
+  return src
+    .split('\n')
+    .filter((line) => {
+      const t = line.trim();
+      return !(t.startsWith('//') || t.startsWith('*') || t.startsWith('/*'));
+    })
+    .join('\n');
+}
+function walk(dir, out = []) {
+  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(path.join(ROOT, dir), { withFileTypes: true })) {
+    const rel = path.join(dir, entry.name);
+    if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(rel, out);
+    else if (/\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(entry.name)) out.push(rel);
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+
+const page = code(read('src/components/PageHeader.tsx'));
+const dash = code(read('src/components/DashboardHeader.tsx'));
+const tabs = code(read('src/components/ResponsiveTabBar.tsx'));
+const drawer = code(read('src/lib/ui/drawerDirection.ts'));
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('1. PageHeader mirrors once AND pins the row');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+check('mirrors the row for Arabic', /flexDirection: isRTL \? 'row-reverse' : 'row'/.test(page));
+check('pins the row to ltr (otherwise Yoga re-flips it)', /direction: 'ltr'/.test(page),
+  'direction: ltr missing — this is the bug');
+check('keeps the leading control first in the tree',
+  /flexDirection[^;]*\n[\s\S]{0,120}?<HamburgerButton plain \/>/.test(page),
+  'hamburger is the first child of the header row');
+check('English branch is untouched: LTR renders a plain `row`',
+  /isRTL \? 'row-reverse' : 'row'/.test(page));
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('2. DashboardHeader keeps the same contract');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+check('mirrors its row', /flexDirection: isRTL \? 'row-reverse' : 'row'/.test(dash));
+check('pins it to ltr', /direction: 'ltr'/.test(dash));
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('3. Other RTL surfaces use the same single-mirror contract');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+check('tab bar mirrors and pins', /isRTL \? 'row-reverse' : 'row'/.test(tabs) && /direction: 'ltr'/.test(tabs));
+check('drawer track places the panel physically',
+  /trackFlexDirection/.test(drawer) && /row-reverse/.test(drawer));
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('4. INVARIANT: no unpinned mirrored row anywhere in src/');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+{
+  const files = walk('src');
+  const offenders = [];
+  for (const rel of files) {
+    const src = code(read(rel));
+    const lines = src.split('\n');
+    lines.forEach((line, i) => {
+      if (!/flexDirection: isRTL \?/.test(line)) return;
+      // The pin may sit just above (same object literal) or on the next lines.
+      const window = lines.slice(Math.max(0, i - 3), i + 8).join('\n');
+      if (!/direction: 'ltr'/.test(window) && !/direction: dir\./.test(window)) {
+        offenders.push(rel + ':' + (i + 1));
+      }
+    });
+  }
+  check('every `flexDirection: isRTL ? ...` row is pinned to ltr',
+    offenders.length === 0,
+    offenders.join(', ') || 'none');
+}
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('5. The leading control clears the edge it actually sits on');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+check('PageHeader: RTL pads with the RIGHT safe-area inset',
+  /paddingRight: isRTL \? rightPad \+ spacing\.sm : rightPad/.test(page));
+check('PageHeader: RTL does not add the leading gap to the left inset',
+  /paddingLeft: isRTL \? leftPad : leftPad \+ spacing\.sm/.test(page));
+check('DashboardHeader: same physical padding rule',
+  /paddingRight: isRTL \? rightPad \+ spacing\.sm : rightPad/.test(dash)
+  && /paddingLeft: isRTL \? leftPad : leftPad \+ spacing\.sm/.test(dash));
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+section('6. The reported screens share the fixed header');
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+for (const screen of [
+  'src/app/(app)/(doctor)/video-library.tsx',
+  'src/app/(app)/(doctor)/students.tsx',
+  'src/app/(app)/(hubs)/credits.tsx',
+  'src/app/(app)/notifications.tsx',
+]) {
+  const src = code(read(screen));
+  check(`${screen.split('/').pop()} renders the shared PageHeader`,
+    /import \{ PageHeader \} from '@\/components\/PageHeader'/.test(src) && /<PageHeader/.test(src));
+  check(`${screen.split('/').pop()} has no hand-rolled hamburger row`,
+    !/HamburgerButton/.test(src));
+}
+
+// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+console.log('\n' + '─'.repeat(60));
+if (failed > 0) {
+  console.error(`${passed} passed, ${failed} FAILED`);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
+console.log(`${passed} passed, 0 failed`);

## Root cause (proven by instrumenting the live request, not inferred)

The web build appended the **file descriptor object** to `FormData` instead of the file:

```
partKind: "[object String]"   partName: "[object Object]"   partSize: null
POST …/storage/upload → 400 {"error":{"code":"upload_missing"}}
```

`toUploadPart()` returns `{ uri, name, type }` — the representation **only React Native** understands, because its native networking layer streams the file from that URI. In a browser, `FormData.append('file', {uri})` follows the HTML spec and stringifies the object, so **no file part existed at all** and PHP correctly answered `upload_missing`. The app printed the size of the *multipart body* next to "فشل الرفع" — that is what 679 / 777 / 790 bytes always were (my run showed 777 B; the path length varies), never the PDF and never picker metadata.

That also explains why the host diagnostics passed, why the parser theory fit, and why the earlier `declared_size_source` work (correct hardening, still in place) changed nothing: the request never carried a document.

## Fix

[uploadPart.ts](src/lib/uploadPart.ts): new `resolveUploadPart()` — on web it fetches the picker's `blob:`/`data:` URL and returns a real `File` (name + MIME preserved), refuses a 0-byte result, and reports an unreadable URI as an actionable error; on native it returns the descriptor unchanged, so streaming from disk is untouched. [php.ts](src/client/php.ts) now awaits it before building `FormData` — which fixes every upload that goes through the storage client (materials **and** avatars) on web, not just this screen.

# MedAcademy — Audit Hybrid PDF Pre-Generation, Priority Queue, and Download Wait-Time UX

Audit the existing MedAcademy PDF watermarking and download pipeline to determine whether the intended hybrid pre-generation and priority-queue system is actually implemented, including accurate waiting-time estimates and a clear student-facing waiting experience.

**IMPORTANT: This is an audit-only task. Do not modify files or production during this investigation.** First establish what is implemented, what is missing, and what needs to change. Base findings on actual code paths, database schema, queue behavior, and tests—not assumptions or comments.

## 1. Intended hybrid PDF processing behavior

### A. Automatic background pre-generation

After a doctor uploads a PDF, the system should automatically schedule personalized PDF copies for eligible students in the background, without requiring each student to press Download first.

Inspect:
- What event schedules pre-generation.
- Which students are eligible and how they are determined.
- Whether jobs are created immediately, lazily, or in batches.
- How already-generated copies are reused.
- How duplicate jobs are prevented.
- Whether background processing is bounded to avoid exhausting shared-hosting resources.

### B. Priority for students requesting downloads

When a student presses Download:

1. If their personalized PDF is already ready, deliver it immediately.
2. If it is not ready, create or promote their job to interactive/high priority.
3. Interactive student download jobs must be processed ahead of background pre-generation jobs that have not started.
4. Jobs already being processed should normally finish safely; do not introduce unsafe cancellation.
5. Preserve authorization and ensure students can only access their own permitted personalized copies.

Inspect whether priority is actually persisted and honored by the database claim logic and worker. Do not assume that adding a priority field alone makes the queue work correctly.

## 2. Student-facing waiting experience

If a student requests a PDF that is not ready, the app must provide a clear, accurate and reassuring experience instead of leaving the student confused or making the download appear broken.

### Required behavior

- Immediately acknowledge the student's request.
- Show a clear Arabic message, such as:

  **"طلبك في قائمة الانتظار"**

  "جاري تجهيز نسخة PDF الخاصة بك، وسنخبرك عندما تصبح جاهزة للتحميل."

# MedAcademy — Database Connection Audit, Safe Optimization, and Authenticated Load Testing

You are working on the existing MedAcademy project, a React Native/Expo application with a PHP backend and MySQL/MariaDB hosted on Spaceship shared hosting.

## Production environment

- API: `https://api.medacademy.site`
- Hosting: Spaceship cPanel shared hosting
- Backend: PHP + MySQL/MariaDB
- Existing load-test tooling: `scripts/loadtest/`
- Existing live capacity report: `scripts/loadtest/LIVE_HOST_CAPACITY_TEST.md`

The latest live test reached 200 concurrent virtual users against four public API endpoints. The first database connection-quota errors appeared at 150 VUs.

The production MariaDB logs reported:

`SQLSTATE[HY000] [1226] User 'vcoafnqsgg_api' has exceeded the 'max_user_connections' resource`

The reported per-user database connection ceiling is 50. At 150 VUs, 13 HTTP 5xx responses were observed; at 200 VUs, 15 were observed. The report also mentioned `max_used_connections=139` and `Threads_connected=62`, but these are server-wide measurements and must not be interpreted as the application's exact connection count.

The previous test used anonymous requests against four public endpoints. It did not establish authenticated student capacity, PDF-generation capacity, or video-streaming capacity.

**Your objective is to identify and safely address the real database connection bottleneck, then validate the improvements using controlled tests.**

## Phase 1 — Inspect the existing implementation

Before changing anything, inspect:

- PHP database connection creation and configuration.
- PDO usage, connection lifetime, transactions and exception handling.
- Every place that opens a new connection or retains a connection longer than necessary.
- Database access inside controllers, services, middleware, queue workers and background scripts.
- Whether multiple connections are opened within a single request unnecessarily.
- Whether connections are reliably released after success, exceptions and early returns.
- Whether persistent PDO connections are enabled and whether they could worsen the shared-hosting connection limit.
- Whether repeated queries or inefficient request paths are causing excessive connection demand.
- The existing load-test runner, scenarios, configuration, reports and tests.
- The existing PHP environment and hosting restrictions, without exposing credentials.

Trace the actual code paths. Do not assume the issue is caused by connection leaks merely because the quota was exceeded.

Produce a baseline diagnosis before implementing changes. Identify the most likely cause or causes and distinguish proven findings from hypotheses.

## Phase 2 — Implement safe, minimal improvements

After documenting the diagnosis, implement only justified changes.

Potential improvements, when supported by the code:
- Reuse the same PDO connection within a single request where appropriate.
- Avoid redundant connection creation within one request.
- Ensure transactions are committed or rolled back correctly.
- Release references to connections and statements when no longer needed.
- Avoid enabling persistent connections as a speculative optimization.
- Reduce unnecessary database round trips.
- Optimize expensive queries only when measurements or query analysis support the change.
- Add bounded timeouts and graceful handling for temporary connection-quota exhaustion where compatible with the current architecture.
- Avoid retry loops that amplify load during database saturation.
- Preserve the existing API contract, authentication, authorization, queue behavior and data integrity.

Do not implement a large connection-pooling system or introduce new infrastructure that is incompatible with ordinary PHP/cPanel shared hosting.

Do not raise `max_user_connections` without confirming that the provider permits it and that the change is justified. Do not edit database server settings or ask for an arbitrary increase merely to make the benchmark pass.

Do not hide connection failures, silently return success, or weaken validation to reduce the error count.

Add regression tests for any corrected connection-lifecycle or error-handling behavior.

## Phase 3 — Production safety and deployment boundaries

Separate local code changes from production deployment.

- Do not deploy backend changes automatically unless the user has explicitly authorized deployment for this task.
- Do not run migrations or modify production data unless required, justified, and explicitly authorized.
- Do not change production cron jobs or database configuration during this phase.
- Do not print or commit passwords, tokens, database credentials or session cookies.
- Do not use real student accounts for load testing.
- Do not create fake student records or bypass production protections to mint test tokens.
- Do not run destructive tests, mass uploads, or unbounded stress tests.
- Do not increase concurrency while the current stage is unhealthy.

If a production smoke test is useful, keep it low-rate and read-only. Run higher-load tests against a staging environment whenever possible.

## Phase 4 — Improve the load-test scenarios

Review and improve the existing load-testing tools under `scripts/loadtest/`.

The test suite must distinguish:

1. Anonymous public API traffic.
2. Authenticated student read-only traffic.
3. PDF availability and download traffic.
4. PDF watermark generation and worker processing.
5. Video metadata/API traffic versus actual video delivery.

Do not combine these workloads into one misleading capacity number.

Use the existing `SESSION_MODE=none` mode only for anonymous testing. For authenticated scenarios, use a dedicated disposable test account on staging or another explicitly authorized test environment.

If no safe test account or staging environment exists, report that limitation and stop short of claiming authenticated capacity. Do not use a real student's identity.

The authenticated scenario should use realistic, bounded request rates and think times, and validate response bodies as well as HTTP status codes.

Do not trigger mass PDF generation against production. For PDF-generation load tests, use a staging environment with representative documents and disposable test users.

## Phase 5 — Run controlled tests

### A. Establish a baseline

Capture:
- HTTP status-code distribution.
- Request count and achieved requests per second.
- p50, p90, p95 and p99 latency.
- Error rate, connection failures and timeouts.
- Per-endpoint request and error breakdown.
- Available database connection counters before and after the run.
- Any observable application or hosting resource metrics.

Clearly label server-wide metrics separately from application-specific metrics.

### B. Verify fixes with a local or staging comparison

Run the same test scenarios before and after the changes under comparable conditions.

Report:
- Whether connection-quota errors decrease.
- Whether latency improves or regresses.
- Whether throughput changes.
- Whether the test harness itself becomes a bottleneck.
- Whether the improvements are repeatable.

### C. Re-test the live public API conservatively

Only after reviewing the baseline and fixing justified code issues, consider a staged live test.

Begin with 2 VUs, then 10, 25, 50, and only consider higher stages when all earlier stages are healthy.

Use short holds initially. Establish conservative stop thresholds before starting:
- HTTP 5xx above 0.5%.
- Overall request error rate above 1%.
- Timeouts above 0.5%.
- p95 latency above 2 seconds, sustained.
- Any clear database quota exhaustion, resource-limit warning or production impact.

If any threshold is exceeded, stop the ramp and allow the system to recover. Do not continue to 150 or 200 merely to reproduce the earlier failure.

These thresholds are initial safeguards, not a guarantee that traffic below them is harmless. Adjust them downward if the baseline or hosting constraints require it.

Never intentionally drive the live shared host to failure.

## Phase 6 — Authenticated student capacity

When a dedicated staging/test account and safe environment are available:

1. Authenticate using the normal application flow.
2. Simulate realistic student sessions with bounded think time.
3. Exercise read-only course and lesson workflows.
4. Validate authorization and response correctness.
5. Test download behavior without creating unlimited files or queue jobs.
6. Test personalized PDF generation separately in staging.
7. Measure the number of concurrent students whose workflows meet the defined latency and error targets.

Report separate capacity findings for:
- Anonymous API traffic.
- Authenticated student browsing.
- PDF downloads.
- PDF generation.
- Video delivery, only if the test actually exercises the video delivery path.

Do not infer video-streaming capacity from API requests or infer PDF-generation capacity from ordinary GET requests.

## Phase 7 — Final report

Produce a detailed report at:

`scripts/loadtest/DATABASE_CONNECTION_AUDIT.md`

Also update `scripts/loadtest/LIVE_HOST_CAPACITY_TEST.md` only when new verified measurements justify doing so.

Include:

1. Root cause analysis with code references.
2. Confirmed findings versus hypotheses.
3. All files modified or created.
4. Tests added and their results.
5. Before-and-after metrics.
6. Database connection-quota evidence.
7. Any available hosting metrics and which metrics are inaccessible.
8. The highest stage that passed without violating safety thresholds.
9. Separate capacity conclusions for each tested workload.
10. Remaining bottlenecks and practical next steps.
11. Deployment requirements and rollback guidance.
12. Every backend file changed or created, plus the exact backend files that must be uploaded to the live server.
13. A clear statement of whether any production deployment, migration, configuration change or cron change occurred.

Run the full project test suite, TypeScript checks and relevant lint/PHP syntax checks. Do not claim success if any relevant test fails; investigate and resolve regressions first.

## Completion criteria

The task is complete when the connection-lifecycle audit is documented, justified fixes are implemented and tested, and controlled benchmarks show whether those fixes materially improve the measured behavior.

Do not claim that MedAcademy supports a particular number of concurrent students unless a representative, authenticated student workload has actually been tested successfully at that concurrency for a meaningful duration.

If authenticated testing cannot safely be performed because staging or test credentials are unavailable, complete the code audit and safe anonymous checks, document the limitation, and specify exactly what is needed to finish the authenticated test.

Start by inspecting the code and existing report. Do not begin by increasing concurrency or changing production database limits.

{"kind":"tool","id":"fUTpF43JtmI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":".freebuff/tools/hold-phase-measure.php","instructions":"Measure the DB-free phases whose connection hold time the fix removes.","content":"<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * hold-phase-measure.php — how much DB connection HOLD TIME each `release()`
 * call site removes, measured rather than asserted.
 *
 * WHY: on a shared host the per-account cap (`max_user_connections = 50`) limits
 * SIMULTANEOUS connections. By Little's law the demand is
 * `requests/second × connection hold time`, so the only thing that matters is how
 * long a request keeps its slot. The three phases below are the slow, DATABASE-FREE
 * parts of the requests that now hand the slot back first:
 *
 *   upload  UploadIntegrityService::inspectStored()  → sha256 of the stored file
 *   deliver MaterialDeliveryController::streamPdf()  → 256 KB chunked send of the PDF
 *   render  MaterialPdfVariantService (watermark)    → the worker's PDF render
 *
 * This is a LOCAL phase measurement on synthetic files of known size. It is NOT a
 * load test and NOT a capacity figure; the report pairs it with the RPS actually
 * observed on the host to estimate how many simultaneous slots the change frees.
 *
 * USAGE  php .freebuff/tools/hold-phase-measure.php [megabytes]
 */

$mb = (int) ($argv[1] ?? 20);
$mb = max(1, min(200, $mb));

$tmp = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/medacademy-hold-phase-' . getmypid() . '.bin';
$fh = fopen($tmp, 'wb');
$chunk = str_repeat('A', 1048576);
for ($i = 0; $i < $mb; $i++) {
    fwrite($fh, $chunk);
}
fclose($fh);
$size = filesize($tmp);

$ms = static fn (float $seconds): string => number_format($seconds * 1000, 1) . ' ms';

// 1 — upload: the hash that must not hold a connection.
$t0 = microtime(true);
$hash = hash_file('sha256', $tmp);
$hashSeconds = microtime(true) - $t0;

// 2 — delivery: 256 KB chunked read, exactly the loop in Http\Response::file().
$t0 = microtime(true);
$in = fopen($tmp, 'rb');
$sink = fopen(PHP_OS_FAMILY === 'Windows' ? 'NUL' : '/dev/null', 'wb');
$bytes = 0;
while (!feof($in)) {
    $buf = fread($in, 262144);
    if ($buf === false || $buf === '') {
        break;
    }
    $bytes += strlen($buf);
    fwrite($sink, $buf);
}
fclose($sink);
fclose($in);
$streamSeconds = microtime(true) - $t0;

printf("file            : %s (%.1f MiB)\n", basename($tmp), $size / 1048576);
printf("sha256          : %s  (%s, %s)\n", substr($hash, 0, 12) . '…', $ms($hashSeconds), number_format($size / max($hashSeconds, 1e-9) / 1048576, 1) . ' MiB/s');
printf("chunked send    : %s  (%s read back, %s)\n", $ms($streamSeconds), number_format($bytes / 1048576, 1) . ' MiB', number_format($size / max($streamSeconds, 1e-9) / 1048576, 1) . ' MiB/s');

unlink($tmp);

// Little's law, stated as arithmetic on measured numbers (not a measurement):
// slots freed per second = request rate × seconds of hold time removed.
$rps = (float) (getenv('OBSERVED_RPS') ?: 0);
echo "\nhold time removed per request : hash " . $ms($hashSeconds) . ' + send ' . $ms($streamSeconds) . "\n";
if ($rps > 0) {
    $hashSlots = $rps * $hashSeconds;
    $sendSlots = $rps * $streamSeconds;
    printf(
        "at the observed %.1f req/s   : ≈%.1f simultaneous slots freed (hash), ≈%.1f (send)\n" .
        "                              (arithmetic on measured values — an estimate, not an observation)\n",
        $rps,
        $hashSlots,
        $sendSlots
    );
} else {
    echo "set OBSERVED_RPS to turn the measured hold times into freed-slot arithmetic.\n";
}

The audit is complete, the justified fixes are implemented and verified locally, and a conservative live re-check was run. Full report: **[scripts/loadtest/DATABASE_CONNECTION_AUDIT.md](scripts/loadtest/DATABASE_CONNECTION_AUDIT.md)**.

## Root cause (confirmed vs inferred)

**Confirmed from code:** there is no connection leak. Exactly one `new PDO` exists in the application ([Database.php:71](backend/src/Database/Database.php#L71)), created lazily, with `PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT` never set, and the singleton holds exactly one connection per request.

**The mechanism:** that single slot used to be held until the script ended — including through phases that touch no database at all. Measured locally: sha256 of a 20 MiB upload = **162 ms**, the 256 KB chunked send = **17.8 ms**, and the watermark render ≈ **0.24 s** per copy. Demand is `requests/s × hold time` against an **account** cap of 50 (`max_user_connections = 50` vs server `max_connections = 500`) — 10× tighter than the server.

**Inferred, not proven:** attributing the 150-VU onset *specifically* to hold time can't be proven from the deployed code, because production still runs the pre-fix code. What is proven is the cap, the one-slot-per-request rule, the hold-time sizes, and that `release()` really returns the slot and reconnects lazily.

## Changes

- **Connection lifecycle:** `Database::release()` (no-op inside a transaction — it can never discard committed work), plus `isConnectionQuotaError()` recognising only 1226/1203/1040, and 5 call sites that hand the slot back before the PDF render, the upload hash/parse, and both file-streaming routes.
- **Honest failure surface:** quota exhaustion now returns `503 database_busy` with `Retry-After: 2` and a `capacity=db_connection_quota` log tag, instead of a generic 500; **no in-request retry**, so load is not amplified. A genuine outage (2002/1045) is not misreported as capacity.
- **Load-test workloads kept apart:** every request now carries a `workload` tag with its own metrics, and the report prints a workload table where an unexercised class shows `**no**` plus its missing precondition instead of borrowing another row's number.

The end-to-end proof is deterministic rather than a race: the test holds the account's whole allowance itself, confirms a third connection is refused with 1226, then asserts the API answers `503 database_busy` + `Retry-After` on every request with **no faked 200**. My first version of that check used `/api/health` — it returned `200 {"status":"degraded"}` six times out of six, because that route catches database errors by design; it now targets a DB-backed route where the failure propagates.

- No production deployment, migration, `.env`/PHP/DB-config or cron change occurred.

# MedAcademy — PDF Watermark Worker Performance, Queue Priority, and Download Load Test

Continue the existing database connection audit and load-testing work. Add a dedicated investigation and test plan for PDF watermark generation, background pre-generation, interactive download priority, and queue processing performance.

## Goals

Determine whether the current PHP worker and database-backed queue can safely process realistic student PDF workloads on the Spaceship shared-hosting environment.

### 1. Inspect the real implementation

Inspect the existing queue service, watermarking service, worker script, worker lock, storage service, download endpoints, relevant migrations and tests.

Trace the actual workflow:
- PDF upload and background pre-generation scheduling.
- Creation and reuse of personalized student copies.
- Interactive download request when a copy is already ready.
- Interactive request when a copy is not ready.
- Queue priority and atomic job claiming.
- Worker time budget and job limits.
- Lock acquisition, overlapping executions and stale-job recovery.
- Failure handling, retry behavior and duplicate-job prevention.
- Student authorization and isolation of personalized copies.

Do not assume any feature works without tracing its actual implementation.

### 2. Build a safe PDF test matrix

Use disposable test users and synthetic or non-sensitive PDFs in a local or staging environment.

Include several representative file sizes, such as 100 KB, 1 MB, 5 MB and 10 MB, but first confirm these sizes are appropriate for the hosting plan and existing application limits.

For each case, record:
- Source file size and SHA-256.
- Queue insertion timestamp.
- Time the worker starts processing.
- Processing duration.
- Time the completed copy becomes available.
- Output file size, PDF validity and watermark verification.
- Whether the generated copy is scoped to the correct test student.
- Errors, retries and duplicate jobs.

Do not upload large batches of test files to production.

### 3. Verify hybrid queue priority

In staging, enqueue background pre-generation jobs, then add interactive download requests.

Verify that:
- Ready copies are reused without unnecessary regeneration.
- Unstarted interactive requests are processed ahead of background jobs.
- Jobs already processing are handled safely.
- Queue ordering is enforced by the actual database claim logic.
- Duplicate requests do not create redundant jobs.
- Interactive jobs cannot starve background jobs indefinitely.
- Worker locking prevents overlapping processing.
- Queue and worker state remain consistent after an exception or simulated worker termination.

Document any deviations from the intended hybrid design.

### 4. Measure worker throughput and queue latency

Run controlled tests with bounded workloads and measure:
- Jobs enqueued, started, completed, retried and failed.
- Queue waiting time and actual processing duration.
- End-to-end time from student request to ready copy.
- Jobs completed per minute.
- Number of jobs processed per worker invocation.
- Time spent waiting for the next cron invocation.
- Database connection failures and other HTTP/API errors.
- Available CPU, memory, PHP process and database metrics, clearly identifying anything unavailable.

Evaluate the existing worker limits (`--limit=5 --max-seconds=50`) against measured processing times. Do not change production limits or cron configuration during the audit.

### 5. Controlled concurrency tests

Prefer staging. Test interactive requests in stages of 1, 5, 10, 20 and 50 virtual students, increasing only while the previous stage remains healthy.

Use representative PDFs and bounded workloads. Do not enqueue unbounded work or intentionally exhaust hosting resources.

Define stop conditions before each run, including:
- Database connection-quota errors.
- Sustained HTTP 5xx errors or timeouts.
- Excessive queue latency or processing failures.
- Abnormal resource consumption or impact on real users.

If staging is unavailable, perform code-level and local tests first. Do not launch a large PDF-generation load test against production without explicit user approval and a documented rollback and cleanup plan.

### 6. Validate student download UX and waiting-time estimates

Trace whether the current frontend and backend:
- Acknowledge a pending request immediately.
- Show an accurate status and server-grounded estimated waiting time.
- Update the status without requiring repeated manual clicks.
- Make the download available when the copy is ready.
- Reuse a ready copy.
- Avoid exposing another student's identity or document information.

Do not display invented fixed estimates. If reliable ETA data is unavailable, recommend a transparent fallback and specify what measurements or API fields are required.

### 7. Final report and implementation boundaries

Write the report to `scripts/loadtest/PDF_WORKER_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT.md`.

Include:
- Verified implementation status.
- Code references and relevant database fields.
- Test environment and workload.
- Source/output validation results.
- Queue latency and worker throughput.
- Before-and-after measurements where applicable.
- Database and hosting resource evidence.
- Bottlenecks and recommended changes.
- Tests added and test results.
- All files changed or created.
- Every backend file that must be uploaded to the live server.
- Deployment, migration and cron requirements, if any.

Do not deploy, modify production configuration, change cron jobs, run migrations or create production test records without explicit authorization.

Do not claim that a particular number of students can download personalized PDFs concurrently unless that exact workload was safely tested with valid measurements.

Start with inspection and a staging/local test plan. If a live production PDF load test is necessary, report the proposed test parameters and request approval before running it.

## What the audit found

**The hybrid design is mostly there, with two real gaps.** Automatic pre-generation (`enqueueMaterial()` fans out prewarm jobs at priority 10), per-student copy reuse (registry + `existing()` short-circuit → `ready:cached`, file mtime unchanged), interactive promotion (`prioritize()` → priority 0), atomic claims, duplicate-job prevention, and the single-instance lock are all **implemented and verified**. Missing: **any waiting-time estimate** (`pdf-status` returns only `retry_after`, a polling interval — no queue position, no ETA) and **aging for prewarm jobs**, so a steady stream of student requests defers background pre-generation indefinitely (measured, not inferred).

**Measured cost per personalized copy** (isolated, median of 3, real FPDI+TCPDF engine): 0.14 s for a 1-page 120 KB file → 1.17 s for a 62-page 11.4 MB file, ≈0.019 s/page beyond ~10 pages, 74 MB peak. The shipped `--limit=5 --max-seconds=50 --min-render-seconds=15` fits comfortably — five 11 MB copies are ~6 s of a 35 s budget — so **`--limit` (5 copies/tick), not render cost, is the ceiling**: ≈300 copies/hour at a one-minute cron.

**Queue at scale** (staged, each of 1/5/10/20/50 simultaneous student requests issued from its own process, drained with the shipped cron shape): every stage created exactly one job per student, no duplicates, no cross-student copies, nothing left in `processing`; at 50 students p50 41.4→41.6 s / p95 66.5→72.2 s, drained in 10 worker runs. Interactive requests are claimed ahead of queued prewarm work, and there is **no permanent starvation but no aging either**.

# MedAcademy — Implement PDF Queue ETA, Persistent Waiting UX, and Prewarm Aging

Use the completed PDF worker audit as the starting point. The audit established that automatic pre-generation, personalized-copy reuse, student priority (0), prewarm priority (10), atomic job claiming, duplicate prevention and worker locking already exist.

The verified gaps are:
1. The client stops waiting after approximately 77–87 seconds even though the cron runs every five minutes, causing healthy queued jobs to appear failed.
2. There is no server-grounded queue position or estimated completion time.
3. The UI does not distinguish queued from actively generating jobs.
4. Prewarm jobs have no aging policy and may be indefinitely deferred under a continuous stream of interactive requests.
5. The Arabic PDF waiting message and transparent ETA fallback are missing.

## Required implementation

### 1. Fix the waiting lifecycle

- Keep the existing ready-copy fast path and automatic download behavior.
- When a student's copy is queued or processing, continue showing a pending state rather than a false failure.
- Make polling behavior consistent with the actual worker schedule and server-provided retry_after.
- Do not show Retry while the job is still healthy and queued or processing.
- Stop polling on ready, terminal failure, unavailable queue, cancellation, or a documented hard timeout with a clear recovery path.
- Avoid duplicate queue jobs and excessive polling.
- Preserve the existing PDF authorization and per-student file isolation.

### 2. Add a server-grounded ETA and queue position

Inspect the actual schema and claim ordering before implementing.

- Compute the number of eligible jobs ahead of the student's job using the real claim order and due-time rules.
- Account for the worker schedule, jobs currently processing, recent successful rendering durations, worker limits and retry delays.
- Use recent successful measurements where sufficient data exists; otherwise return a null ETA rather than inventing one.
- Return a conservative estimate or range when the data supports one.
- Do not mistake retry_after (the next polling interval) for the estimated completion time.
- Keep queries bounded and efficient, using existing indexes wherever possible.
- Do not introduce a migration unless code inspection proves it is necessary.

Extend the existing pdf-url and pdf-status response shapes consistently. Clearly distinguish queued, generating, ready, failed and unavailable states while preserving backward compatibility with existing clients.

### 3. Update the student UI and localization

Add localized Arabic and English messages for:
- Queued: "طلبك في قائمة الانتظار"
- Description: "جاري تجهيز نسخة PDF الخاصة بك، وسنحدّثك عندما تصبح جاهزة للتحميل."
- ETA range when available.
- Unknown ETA fallback: "الوقت المتوقع غير متاح حاليًا، وسنحدّث الحالة تلقائيًا."
- Actively generating.
- Recoverable versus terminal failures.

Display queue position only when it is meaningful and safe. Do not expose other students' identities or private job information.

Preserve automatic download when ready, RTL/LTR behavior, responsive layouts and the existing visual design.

### 4. Prevent indefinite prewarm starvation

Design a bounded aging policy so background pre-generation jobs can gradually gain priority after waiting sufficiently long, without allowing them to block new interactive student requests unfairly.

Inspect the existing priority and atomic claim SQL before proposing or implementing aging. Prefer a minimal indexed solution that is safe under concurrent workers. Add tests proving:
- Interactive requests normally outrank unstarted prewarm jobs.
- Old prewarm jobs eventually progress under sustained interactive load.
- Aged prewarm jobs do not starve interactive requests.
- Atomic claims, duplicate prevention and worker locking remain correct.

Do not change production worker concurrency or cron settings as part of code implementation.

### 5. Worker schedule and configuration

The live cron currently runs every five minutes. Keep the ETA calculation consistent with the configured worker interval. If adding a configuration value, default it to the currently verified five-minute interval and document how it must be changed if the owner later changes cron to every minute.

Do not change live cron configuration or claim that the cron runs every minute unless it has actually been changed and verified.

### 6. Tests and deployment

Add tests for ETA calculation, queue ordering, all API states, client polling behavior, ETA fallback, retry semantics, and prewarm aging.

Run the relevant PHP queue/delivery/worker suites, JavaScript tests, TypeScript checks and focused linting. Report any test that could not run because of missing local dependencies.

Do not deploy automatically. Do not run migrations or alter production data. Preserve the existing API contract wherever possible.

At completion, provide:
- Root cause and implementation summary.
- Every file modified or created.
- Test results.
- Every backend file that must be uploaded to the live server.
- Any frontend web rebuild requirement.
- Any required cron/configuration change, clearly marked as a separate owner action.
- Rollback instructions.

Do not claim that the ETA is accurate until it has been validated against actual queue wait times. Do not claim that the hybrid behavior is complete until the new tests pass.

Begin by reviewing the existing diff and audit report to avoid overwriting or duplicating the earlier database connection fixes. Implement the PDF waiting/ETA and prewarm-aging changes only; keep database connection improvements separate for their own deployment review.

### 6.3 Aging: background pre-generation cannot be deferred forever

`claim()` orders strictly `priority ASC` — correct for waiting students, but it
meant that while student requests kept arriving, upload pre-generation waited
indefinitely (measured: see `scripts/loadtest/PDF_WORKER_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT.md`
§7 C5). The fix is bounded rather than a priority inversion:

* only `priority >= 10` (prewarm) rows are eligible — a waiting student (0)
  **always** outranks them, so interactive work is never starved;
* only a row already older than `MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_STARVATION_SECONDS`;
* the **oldest** such row is taken first, so no single background job can be left
  permanently behind newer ones;
* at most `MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_RESERVED_CLAIMS` **per worker run**, claimed
  *before* the interactive batch, so the slot is never lost to the run's budget.
  With `--limit=5` that is at most one of five renders, and only after 15 min.

The claim itself is unchanged and still atomic
(`WHERE status = 'queued'` + lock token), so a second worker cannot double-claim.

The app (`src/app/(app)/lesson/[id].tsx`, rules in `src/lib/pdfPreparation.ts`)

The ETA, waiting UX and prewarm aging are implemented, tested and verified locally. No deployment, no migration, no cron change.

## Root causes fixed

**1. The client abandoned healthy jobs.** The old loop polled at most 10 times (10 s then 8 s ≈ **82 s total**) while the worker runs on a five-minute cron, so a student who arrived just after a tick was shown "Download Failed" for a copy that was still queued. The polling budget is now a function of the deployed schedule: floor 5 s, ×1.6 growth, ceiling 20 s, honouring a longer server `retry_after`, with a **15-minute hard deadline** (three five-minute ticks) — and when that deadline passes the app shows "still queued" with a *Check again* action instead of a failure. Retry (which re-queues) is offered **only** for a terminal failure; re-checking passes `retry: false`.

**2. No queue information existed.** `pdf-url`/`pdf-status` returned only `retry_after` (a polling interval) and `reason`. They now return a grounded wait contract: `state` (`queued`/`generating`/`ready`/`failed`/`unavailable`), `queue_position`, `jobs_ahead`, `processing_now`, and `eta_seconds`/`eta_min_seconds`/`eta_max_seconds`/`eta_basis`/`eta_samples`. The estimate = `worker interval` + `jobs/run` + the job's own `run_after` + the **median of measured render durations** (`ready_at − locked_at`, last 7 days, ≤50 samples); with fewer than 3 measurements **every ETA field is null** and the app shows the transparent fallback instead of a number. The range is exactly one worker interval wide (next tick may be imminent or a full interval away) and `eta_seconds` is the conservative upper bound; `retry_after` is never used as an ETA.

**3. Prewarm could be deferred forever.** Strict `priority ASC` meant a continuous student stream starved background pre-generation (measured in the audit, §7 C5). Aging is now bounded rather than a priority inversion: a prewarm job older than `MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_STARVATION_SECONDS` (900) gets **one reserved claim per run** (`MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_RESERVED_CLAIMS`, max 2), taken **before** the interactive batch, oldest first, never the whole run (`--limit=1` reserves nothing), and never a priority-0 row. Students always outrank unstarted prewarm work.

## Files

Backend: [MaterialPdfQueueService.php](backend/src/Services/MaterialPdfQueueService.php) (states, estimate, `claimAgedPrewarm`, `health()` aging counters; `markReady` now **keeps `locked_at`** — that stamp pair is the render measurement, and every claim/stale path still requires `status='processing'`), [MaterialDeliveryController.php](backend/src/Controllers/MaterialDeliveryController.php) (one `waitFields()` shared by both endpoints, `clientStatus()` keeps the three-value contract), [watermark-worker.php](backend/scripts/watermark-worker.php) (reserved slot first, `--prewarm-reserved`, summary counter), [.env.example](backend/.env.example) and [PDF_WATERMARK_QUEUE.md](backend/docs/PDF_WATERMARK_QUEUE.md) (§4.1 cadence config, §6.1–6.4 contract, estimate, aging, polling).

Tests: new [pdf_wait_estimate_tests.php](backend/tests/material-queue/pdf_wait_estimate_tests.php) (DB-backed E1–E10), new [materialPdfWaiting.test.cjs](tests/materialPdfWaiting.test.cjs) (compiles and **executes** the rules + contract/localization assertions), new P10 aging phase in [pdf_worker_performance_tests.php](backend/tests/material-queue/pdf_worker_performance_tests.php), and [materialPdfQueue.test.cjs](tests/materialPdfQueue.test.cjs) updated to the new budget.

## Test results (all on the final tree)

`pdf_wait_estimate_tests.php` **36 checks, 0 failed** — it caught a real bug in my first draft (`+` never overwrites, so `eta_basis` overrides were dropped; now `array_merge`). Perf suite (100k,1m) **48 passed / 0 skipped / 0 failed**, including P10: a `--limit=1` run serves the waiting student, a `--limit=2` run serves the starved background job first (details[0] = my aged prewarm job, `prewarm_reserved: 1`) and still completes both. `queue_tests.php` **50 checks, 0 failed**; `worker_lock_tests.php` all passed; concurrency suite (stages 1,5) **20 passed, 0 failed** (C5 correctly still shows a *young* prewarm job deferred — only aged ones are rescued). Local MariaDB is running (port 3307), so all DB-backed suites ran; leftovers cleaned (0 `qtest` rows; I also removed 40 MB of stray `qtest-*` copy folders left by an earlier session's concurrency run).

## What I did NOT verify, and the honest ETA caveat

The ETA has **not** been validated against real end-to-end queue waits in production. It is structurally verified (width = one interval, learns from measurement, class-aware, never shorter than `run_after`, null without samples), and it is deliberately conservative: with `interval=300`, `jobs/run=5`, `reserved=1`, a one-job interactive copy reports **4 s – 304 s** where the measured local drain p50/p95 was 0.14 s/1.14 s — i.e. it models the worst-case cron phase, not the average. No live or staging authenticated run was made (production has no disposable student account), and no visual/browser check of the modal was performed; those remain the user's to do.

A **new frontend bundle is required** (the client changed); rollback is safe either way because the new app degrades to the unknown-ETA fallback against an old backend, and setting `MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_RESERVED_CLAIMS=0` restores strict interactive-first ordering without touching files.

The one design decision worth your review: `markReady()` no longer clears `locked_at`, which the earlier performance test's comment described as "holds no lock" — the invariant it guards (no `lock_token`, and `status='processing'` required everywhere) is intact, and that stamp is what makes a measured render duration possible at all.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * run-state-tests.cjs — compiles the PURE, dependency-free state models
 * (src/lib/securityStateModel.ts, src/lib/startupStateModel.ts,
 * src/lib/maintenanceStateModel.ts) standalone and hands the compiled
 * CommonJS modules to the test files in tests/.
 *
 * WHY THIS IS TRACKED (was .freebuff/run-state-tests.cjs)
 * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The runner used to live in `.freebuff/`, which `.gitignore` excludes — so
 * `npm run test:state` could not run from a clean checkout, and the compiled
 * models it produces were unavailable to four suites that require them. The
 * harness is not secret, contains no credentials and depends only on node
 * built-ins plus the repo's own `typescript`; it belongs in `scripts/` with the
 * other validation tooling.
 *
 * Output goes to `scripts/state-build/` (git-ignored, regenerated every run).
 * The tests resolve the compiled models from `scripts/state-build` first and
 * fall back to the legacy `.freebuff/state-build` so nothing that already
 * existed on a developer machine breaks.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/run-state-tests.cjs                 # default state/offline suites
 *   node scripts/run-state-tests.cjs <file> [file…]  # specific tests/*.cjs files
 *
 * Exit code is non-zero if any suite fails (failures are never swallowed).
 */

'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { spawnSync } = require('child_process');
const { buildStateModels } = require('./state-build-models.cjs');

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');

// Suites that consume the compiled models (plus the offline regression set that
// used to be wired to the now-missing .freebuff/run-offline-tests.cjs).
const DEFAULT_TESTS = [
  'securityStateModel.test.cjs',
  'offlineState.test.cjs',
  'maintenanceMode.test.cjs',
];

function run(testFile) {
  const proc = spawnSync(process.execPath, [testFile], { stdio: 'inherit' });
  return proc.status ?? 1;
}

const TESTS_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'tests');
const requested = process.argv.slice(2);
const testFiles = requested.length > 0 ? requested : DEFAULT_TESTS;

let exit = 0;
try {
  buildStateModels();
} catch (e) {
  console.error('state-build failed:', e.message);
  process.exit(1);
}

for (const f of testFiles) {
  const p = path.isAbsolute(f) ? f : path.join(TESTS_DIR, f);
  if (!fs.existsSync(p)) {
    console.error(`state-test file not found: ${f}`);
    exit = exit || 1;
    continue;
  }
  const code = run(p);
  if (code !== 0) exit = code;
}
process.exit(exit);

-- ============================================================================
-- 038_pdf_watermark_queue.sql
--
-- Durable, bounded queue for personalized (watermarked) lesson-PDF copies.
--
-- WHY
--   Generating a student's personalized copy used to happen INSIDE the
--   `/materials/pdf-url` request. On cPanel shared hosting a handful of
--   simultaneous first-opens of the same large PDF therefore held PHP-FPM
--   workers for the whole render, and every student paid that latency on their
--   first open. The queue moves generation into a short-lived CLI worker run
--   from cron, so a student's first request never renders a PDF inline.
--
-- WHAT THIS ADDS
--   `lesson_material_pdf_jobs` — one row per (material, student, variant) that
--   still needs a copy. `variant_key` is the SAME identity the delivery path
--   uses (source hash + student identity + engine settings), so a replaced
--   source PDF or a settings change produces a NEW job instead of silently
--   reusing a stale copy.
--
--   status: queued | processing | ready | failed | skipped
--     • queued     — waiting; `run_after` is the retry backoff gate.
--     • processing — claimed by a worker; `lock_token` identifies the claim so
--                    a worker only ever finishes jobs IT claimed.
--     • ready      — the copy exists in the registry (`lesson_material_pdfs`).
--     • failed     — `max_attempts` exhausted; a student retry re-queues it.
--     • skipped    — no longer eligible (unpublished, suspended enrollment,
--                    material hidden/deleted, source changed). Terminal.
--
-- SAFETY
--   • Additive only: one new table, no existing column or row is touched.
--   • The UNIQUE key (material_id, student_id, variant_key) is what prevents
--     duplicate jobs — concurrent uploads/requests cannot create two renders of
--     the same copy.
--   • Foreign keys cascade, so deleting a material or a profile cannot leave a
--     job pointing at nothing.
--
-- HOW TO APPLY (LATER — not applied to production by this change)
--   phpMyAdmin → select the MedAcademy database → Import → choose this file,
--   OR paste it into the SQL tab. Run it ONCE.
--   Re-running is harmless: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.
--
-- TO ROLL BACK
--   See 038_pdf_watermark_queue_down.sql. Dropping the queue table loses only
--   the queue state; generated copies stay in `lesson_material_pdfs` and remain
--   deliverable, and a later request re-creates a job if a copy is missing.
-- ============================================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `lesson_material_pdf_jobs` (
  `id`            CHAR(36)     NOT NULL,
  `material_id`   CHAR(36)     NOT NULL,
  `student_id`    CHAR(36)     NOT NULL,
  -- sha256 of the SOURCE pdf this job must personalize.
  `source_hash`   CHAR(64)     NOT NULL,
  -- sha256(source_hash + identity + engine settings) — same formula as
  -- MaterialPdfVariantService, so job and cache identity can never drift.
  `variant_key`   CHAR(64)     NOT NULL,
  `status`        VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued',
  -- Lower runs first. 0 = a student is waiting on this copy right now,
  -- 10 = upload-time pre-generation for enrolled students.

### Root cause and implementation summary

**1. Client abandoned healthy queued jobs.** The old poll loop maxed out at ~82 s (10 attempts with decreasing delays) while the worker cron runs every 5 minutes. A student arriving just after a tick saw their queued copy reported as "Download Failed" before the next cron tick. **Fix**: hard 15-minute budget (`PDF_POLL_MAX_WAIT_MS = 15 min` = three 5-min ticks), with `nextPollDelay` growing from 5 s floor to 20 s ceiling, honouring server `retry_after` beyond the ceiling, and showing "still queued" with a *Check again* action instead of failure when the budget expires.

**2. No server-grounded wait information.** `pdf-url`/`pdf-status` only returned `retry_after` (a polling interval) with no queue position or ETA. **Fix**: `statusFor()` now returns `state` (`queued`/`generating`/`ready`/`failed`/`unavailable`), `queue_position` / `jobs_ahead` (real rank in worker claim order `priority ASC, run_after ASC, created_at ASC`), `processing_now`, and `eta_*` derived from measured render durations (`ready_at - locked_at`, median of last 50 samples from the last 7 days, requiring ≥3 samples). With fewer than 3 measurements, every `eta_*` is `null` and the app shows the transparent fallback "estimated time not available right now; status will update automatically."

**3. Prewarm could be deferred indefinitely.** Strict `priority ASC` meant a continuous student stream could starve background pre-generation forever (observed in the performance audit). **Fix**: bounded aging policy — a prewarm job older than `MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_STARVATION_SECONDS` (900 s) earns **one reserved claim per worker run** (`MATERIAL_PDF_PREWARM_RESERVED_CLAIMS`, max 2), claimed **before** the interactive batch (`--limit=1` per slot), oldest first. Students (priority 0) always outrank unstarted prewarm work. Aged prewarm jobs gradually gain priority without blocking new interactive requests.

**4. Client polling was inconsistent with the worker schedule.** **Fix**: `PDF_POLL_MAX_WAIT_MS = 15 * 60 * 1_000` (three five-minute ticks), growth factor 1.6× per poll capped at 20 s, server `retry_after` honoured beyond the ceiling, budget exhaustion shows "still queued" with *Check again* — never a false failure.

**5. Arabic localization missing.** **Fix**: 14 new translation keys in both English and Arabic, including the exact Arabic queue message "طلبك في قائمة الانتظار", the description "جاري تجهيز نسخة PDF الخاصة بك، وسنخبرك عندما تصبح جاهزة للتحميل.", and the unknown-ETA fallback "الوقت المتوقع غير متاح حاليًا، وسنحدّث الحالة تلقائيًا."

- Simplified worker to on-demand only (removed prewarm reservation/aging); stale variant re-enqueue behavior preserved
- Updated retention logic to use `created_at` (fixed 24h), active-job protection preserved
- Updated tests and docs to reflect 24h retention and on-demand-only behavior

**Changed files:**
- backend/src/Controllers/LessonMaterialController.php
- backend/src/Services/MaterialPdfQueueService.php
- backend/src/Services/MaterialPdfVariantService.php
- backend/scripts/watermark-worker.php

- Existing personalized PDFs remain until sweep deletes them by 24h-from-generation rule (using `created_at`). Pre-generated copies from before this change will expire per the new 24h window.
- Existing prewarm jobs in queue remain but worker no longer gives them special treatment; they will be processed if claimed (with normal priority) or can age out naturally. No new prewarm jobs will be enqueued.
- Cleanup preserves original source materials; only personalized copies in `lesson-material-pdfs/{course}/{material}/{student}/` are removed by retention/sweep.

- Any code paths calling `enqueueMaterial()` elsewhere would now be no-ops (we searched and disabled known paths).
- If cron/workers are running, ensure updated worker deployed so prewarm reservation logic isn't used.

# Focused final audit: strict on-demand PDF implementation

## 1) Trace: student PDF request → generation → delivery (current code)

**Endpoint:** `POST /materials/pdf-url` (MaterialDeliveryController::pdfUrl)  
**Auth/flow:**
1. Rate limit per account (`material_pdf_mint`), load material, enforce access via `StorageService::canAccess()` (same policy as storage), run integrity check via `IntegrityService::assertActionAllowed()` for `material_pdf`, call `$this->shouldWatermark($role)` (unconditional). 
2. Get identity via `MaterialPdfVariantService::identity($material, $userId)` (throws 404 if source missing, 403 if no profile). 
3. Fast path: `variants->existing($material, $userId, $identity['variant_key'])` returns copy if valid (source hash matches, file exists). If found, call `$variants->touchServed($copy)` and return `readyResponse()` with short-lived URL. 
4. **Staff/doctor/admin/super_admin:** if `isStaff($role)`, call `variants->ensure($material, $userId)` synchronously (inline render), touch served, return ready. 
5. **Student:** if retry requested call `$queue->retry()`. Call `$queue->prioritize($material, $userId, true)` to enqueue/create job (priority STUDENT). If null throw 503. Get status via `$queue->statusFor()`. Re-check for copy (race between enqueue and worker finishing) - if exists return ready. Otherwise return `pendingResponse()` with queued/generating state + wait fields/ETA.

**Delivery/streaming:** `GET /materials/pdf` (MaterialDeliveryController::streamPdf) re-authorizes via `canAccess()` on every request, looks up copy by variant key, streams from `lesson-material-pdfs` bucket; refuses if missing (never serves original). `GET /materials/pdf-status` returns read-only status with wait contract.

**Generation implementation:** `MaterialPdfVariantService::ensure()` does identity check, fast-path lookup, acquires per-variant file lock, double-checks inside lock, releases DB connection during render, renders to `.part` file, verifies (PDF header + %%EOF, size>=1KB), renames atomically, calls `registerVariant()` to upsert into `lesson_material_pdfs`, purges stale variants for same student/material, returns copy metadata. `registerVariant()` sets `created_at` and `updated_at` on insert/update.

## 2) Synchronous or enqueued?

**Students: ENQUEUED (async) via queue.** Generation happens in background worker, not in the HTTP request. Staff are synchronous (inline). The frontend polls via `getMaterialPdfStatus()` and re-calls `getMaterialPdfUrl()` until ready (with bounded budget per pdfPreparation.ts).

## 3) Remaining PDF cron/worker responsibilities

**Watermark worker (`backend/scripts/watermark-worker.php`):**
- Claims jobs via `MaterialPdfQueueService::claim(1, $workerId)` (we simplified from prewarm reservation)
- For each job: load material, check if PDF, re-check eligibility (`isStudentEligible()`), get identity, if variant changed mark skipped and re-enqueue with original priority; if copy already exists mark ready; else call `variants->ensure($material, $studentId)`, mark ready or handle lock loss
- On shutdown/fatal releases held job
- **Stale recovery:** `recoverStale($staleSeconds)` marks processing jobs with expired locks as failed (if attempts>=max) or requeues (with backoff)
- **Retention cleanup:** when called with `--retention --apply` runs `sweepRetention()` to delete expired copies

**Queue service responsibilities:**
- Job enqueueing/deduplication/prioritization, atomic claiming, retries with backoff, stale recovery, status/ETA calculation, retention sweep (`sweepRetention()` deletes from `lesson_material_pdfs` where `created_at < cutoff` and no active job, only within `{course}/{material}/{student}/` prefix, never touches originals)
- Prewarm fanout disabled (enqueueMaterial returns no-op)

**Cron dependency:** Generation/retries/stale recovery require worker. Retention cleanup requires worker run with `--retention`. Without cron, queued jobs won't be processed and cleanup won't run automatically.

## 4) What breaks if PDF cron is removed?

- **Student requests hang in pending:** jobs enqueued by prioritize() won't be processed; clients poll until budget exhausted → show "still queued" state, no PDF delivered
- **Retries after failures won't be processed** (retry() only requeues jobs)
- **Stale locks won't be recovered** (jobs stuck in processing)
- **Retention cleanup won't run** → expired personalized PDFs accumulate on disk/DB (24h retention not enforced automatically)
- **No automatic processing of any queued on-demand jobs**

## 5) Existing queued prewarm jobs - safe handling

**Current state:** We disabled prewarm enqueue paths. Existing rows in `lesson_material_pdf_jobs` with `priority >= 10` (PREWARM) and status queued/processing remain in DB. They would be claimed by worker and processed (consuming capacity). 

**Safe approach (no production deletion without approval):**
1. **Identify:** Query for prewarm jobs: `SELECT * FROM lesson_material_pdf_jobs WHERE priority >= 10 AND status IN ('queued','processing')`
2. **Prevent processing without deleting rows/files:** Mark them as skipped/failed so worker won't waste resources and they won't block on-demand jobs. Options:
   - Update to `status='skipped'`, set `last_error='prewarm_disabled'` (preserves history)

Fix the MedAcademy personalized PDF watermarking pipeline. The currently generated PDF is incorrect: it contains many repeated watermarks scattered across every page. This is explicitly unacceptable.

Follow these exact requirements. Inspect the actual implementation and fix the root cause rather than applying a superficial patch.

## 1. Exactly ONE watermark per page
- Render exactly one personalized watermark on each page.
- Place it at the exact center of the page, both horizontally and vertically.
- The watermark must contain the intended student's identity, such as their name and student/public ID, according to the existing identity configuration.
- Use a subtle, semi-transparent gray appearance that remains readable over both text and images.
- Do not tile, repeat, scatter, rotate into multiple copies, or place additional watermarks in corners, margins, headers, or footers.
- Remove any duplicate watermarking stages. Audit FPDI/TCPDF watermark drawing, page templates, imported PDF overlays, loops, and all other watermark insertion paths. Ensure the watermark is applied exactly once per output page.

## 2. Rasterize AFTER applying the watermark
The required processing order is:

1. Load the original source PDF.
2. Render each original page at a suitable, configurable resolution (target approximately 200–250 DPI, balancing readability, output size, and server memory).
3. Composite exactly one centered personalized watermark into that page image.
4. Encode each completed page as a raster image, with the watermark permanently baked into its pixels.
5. Create a new PDF from those completed page images, preserving page order, page dimensions/aspect ratios, and portrait/landscape orientation.
6. Ensure the resulting PDF pages contain only the rasterized page imagery, not the original searchable text, vector objects, or a separate watermark text/object layer.
7. Validate the final PDF before publishing it atomically.

Do not merely add images over the original PDF while leaving the original text/vector content underneath. Do not append a second watermark during final PDF assembly.

## 3. Verify the output objectively
Create an automated regression test using a multi-page fixture with known page content. Verify:

- Each page contains exactly one visually detectable watermark at the center.
- There are no repeated watermark copies around the page.
- The watermark remains visible but does not obstruct reading.
- The final PDF has the expected page count and correct orientation.
- Normal PDF text extraction does not recover the original selectable text.
- The watermark is embedded in the page pixels rather than represented as a separate text or vector overlay.
- There is no original searchable-text layer underneath the raster images.
- The generated PDF opens successfully and all pages render correctly.
- Different students receive separately watermarked copies with the correct identities.
- Repeated requests reuse the correct existing copy and never return another student's copy.

Use image-based validation and inspect rendered output pages, not just PDF metadata or successful return codes.

Important: rasterization prevents ordinary selectable-text extraction, but OCR can still recognize text from images. Do not claim that OCR-based extraction is impossible.

## 4. Performance, storage, and compatibility
- Preserve the existing PHP backend and compatible, properly licensed PDF/image-processing dependencies.
- Inspect available rendering tools and their actual server availability before selecting an implementation.
- Avoid loading an entire large PDF into memory at once; process pages incrementally and enforce safe resource limits.
- Preserve the agreed on-demand-only behavior: never pre-generate personalized PDFs before a student requests one.
- Preserve the 24-hour retention rule for generated copies.
- Preserve authorization, per-student isolation, duplicate-generation locks, atomic file publication, and failure cleanup.
- Do not change cron configuration, production files, database records, or deploy anything without approval.
- Do not permanently modify generated `ios/` files. Use npm and package-lock.json if frontend dependencies are relevant; never use pnpm.

## 5. Final deliverables
Report:
1. The exact root cause of the repeated watermarks.
2. Every file changed or created.
3. The rendering and rasterization implementation selected and why.
4. Test results and before/after rendered page comparisons.
5. Performance and output-size measurements for both small and large PDFs.
6. Every backend file that must be deployed to production.

Do not mark the task complete until the generated output has been visually inspected and the automated tests prove that the repeated-watermark defect is fixed.

Two harness defects were found and fixed while re-running this, neither a
product bug:

1. **`flatten_engine_tests.php` was not hermetic.** The inherited
   `PDF_WATERMARK_MODE` / `PDF_WATERMARK_OPACITY` in `$_ENV` (populated at
   process start) takes precedence over `putenv()`, so the suite could silently
   run in the wrong engine mode depending on the caller's environment. It now
   sets/restores both `$_ENV` and `putenv()` and calls `Config::init()`.
2. **`delivery_tests.php` had a stale stat cache.** The cleanup assertions
   stat()ed the orphan file in the parent process, then a *child* process
   deleted it; PHP's stat cache still answered "exists", so
   `cleanup: --apply removes the orphaned file` failed on a correct delete.
   The check now calls `clearstatcache(true, $orphan)` first.

Both were test-harness issues: the delivered bytes, the authorization decisions
and the cleanup behaviour were already correct. The exact command and full
machine-readable output are recorded in the companion
[`PDF_WATERMARK_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md`](PDF_WATERMARK_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md)
and the ignored `.freebuff/pdf-watermark-tests/out/` artifacts.","allowMultiple":false}]}}

# Workstream 1 — Restore direct on-demand PDF generation

## Required behavior

Remove the student-facing PDF queue/waiting workflow and restore direct, on-demand generation.

For each student/material combination:

- If a valid, completed, personalized PDF exists and is less than 24 hours old, return that exact cached copy immediately without rendering it again.
- If no valid copy exists, or the cached copy has expired, generate a new personalized PDF as part of the student's request, then return it and retain the completed copy for 24 hours.
- The user should not get stuck in an indefinite “queued,” “waiting,” or “generating” state.
- Do not require a scheduled cron execution to start or complete PDF generation.
- Ensure expired copies are no longer served. Preserve appropriate cleanup of expired files and database records without introducing unbounded storage growth.
- Make concurrent requests for the same student/material safe: prevent duplicate rendering and prevent one student's PDF from ever being delivered to another student.
- Use bounded resource usage and appropriate timeout/error handling. Do not introduce unlimited synchronous rendering or retry loops.
- Preserve authorization, access checks, identity validation, watermarking, atomic file publication, and cleanup after failures.

Review every relevant API endpoint, frontend polling/state component, queue service, cache/variant service, worker, and test. Remove obsolete queue-dependent student behavior only after replacing it with a working direct-generation flow.

Do not blindly delete the queue infrastructure if it is still required by another supported workflow. Clearly identify obsolete code versus infrastructure still needed for locking, retention, cleanup, or backward compatibility.

## Watermark requirements

Preserve the latest intended watermark implementation:

- Exactly one student identity watermark per PDF page.
- Centered horizontally and vertically, subtle semi-transparent gray, readable without obscuring the content.
- Rasterize each page and publish a new image-based PDF, with no original searchable/vector text layer remaining underneath.
- Preserve page count, page order, rotation, aspect ratio, legibility, and reasonable output size.
- Process pages incrementally where practical to avoid excessive memory usage.
- Verify that watermarking is applied only once.
- Preserve student-specific isolation and the existing Ghostscript licensing/prerequisite gate. Never bypass the licensing check or silently fall back to the old repeated vector-watermark renderer.

Inspect the actual renderer availability and licensing assumptions before changing renderer selection. Do not claim production readiness based only on local tests.

## PDF tests

Add or update tests to cover:

- Existing unexpired copy reused without rendering.
- Expired copy regenerated.
- Missing copy generated immediately during the request.
- No student-facing queue/polling deadlock.
- Concurrent duplicate requests and lock recovery.
- Different students never share a personalized PDF.
- Exactly one centered watermark per page.
- Image-only output with no extractable original text layer.
- Correct 24-hour retention and expired-copy cleanup.
- Failures release locks/resources and do not publish incomplete files.

# Workstream 2 — Global startup and app performance audit (highest priority)

The app currently takes too long to open even when the internet connection is fast. Returning to the app from the background can also be slow, and sometimes the app displays a verification failure or a similar error, or fails to open.

Do not assume the network is the cause. Profile the entire startup and re-entry path.

## Audit all startup stages

Trace and measure:

- Native launch and JavaScript initialization.
- Expo Router initialization and route guards.
- Authentication/session restoration.
- SecurityGate and server/device verification.
- API requests and their dependency chains.
- User profile, permissions, courses, and dashboard initialization.
- Secure storage reads, token refresh, and session validation.
- Font, image, and other asset loading.
- Repeated effects, duplicate API calls, unnecessary renders, and expensive synchronous operations.
- AppState/background-to-foreground transitions.
- Timeout handling and navigation behavior after failed requests.

Record measurable timings before and after fixes where possible. Distinguish cold start, warm start, and foreground re-entry.

## Implement targeted performance fixes

- Eliminate redundant API calls and duplicate initialization.
- Run independent requests concurrently where safe.
- Cache suitable non-sensitive data and reuse it when still valid.
- Define clear cache invalidation and refresh behavior so users do not see indefinitely stale permissions, account state, or course access.
- Avoid blocking the first usable screen on nonessential data.
- Prevent splash/loading screens from remaining indefinitely.
- Optimize expensive rendering and image/list loading without changing intended functionality.
- Avoid re-running the entire startup sequence on every foreground event unless required.
- Ensure session restoration and security verification have explicit, bounded timeout behavior.
- Handle temporary connectivity errors and server failures gracefully with bounded retries and useful recovery options.
- Do not repeatedly retry failed requests in a way that amplifies server load.
- Prevent race conditions between authentication, verification, session restoration, and navigation.
- Fix the actual root cause of intermittent verification failures rather than merely changing the error message or automatically bypassing the check.

If verification depends on a server endpoint, inspect both client and backend behavior, request timing, error classification, caching policy, and logs. Never treat an unknown verification result as success.

## Performance validation

Measure and report:

- Cold launch time.
- Warm launch/re-entry time.
- Time to first usable screen.
- Number of requests made during startup.
- Duplicate requests eliminated.
- Verification success/failure behavior during temporary network loss.
- Memory/rendering problems discovered.
- Before/after timings from comparable test conditions.

Test fresh login, an existing authenticated session, expired credentials, background/foreground transitions, slow network, offline mode, and server errors. Do not claim improvement without evidence.

    /showPrepareFailure\(name, materialId, forDownload\)/.test(lesson)
    && /runId !== pdfRunRef\.current/.test(lesson));

    /if \(state === 'unavailable'\) \{[\s\S]{0,400}?break;/.test(lesson));

    /export type MaterialPdfState = 'queued' \| 'generating' \| 'ready' \| 'failed' \| 'unavailable'/.test(api)
